output.user_reply: It appears that the issue you're experiencing is a known limitation in Streamlit where it does not handle PermissionError on Windows when the default port 8501 is reserved by the system. Instead of auto-searching for the next available port, it crashes. This behavior has been noted in previous discussions, and it seems that the application only checks for EADDRINUSE errors. A potential solution would be to modify the exception handling to include PermissionError as well, but this would require changes in the Streamlit codebase. I recommend checking if there is a newer version of Streamlit available that may have addressed this issue. You can also manually specify a different port using the `--server.port` option when running your app. Please refer to the related issue [S1] for more context.

You can do this by modifying your `pyproject.toml` or requirements file accordingly. If you have any further questions or need assistance with this, feel free to ask!
